Strip footing on sand: you verify bearing failure with an ultimate-pressure formula and serviceability with a settlement calculation.
A separate calculation model for each limit state: the direct method.
A small family house: you estimate the bearing resistance from the cone resistance of a CPT with an empirical formula.
Comparable experience and field measurement: the indirect method – in Geotechnical Category 1 and partly 2.
Bridge abutment founded on intact granite: you take an allowable contact pressure from the type, discontinuities and uniaxial compressive strength of the rock.
Presumed bearing resistance on rock: the prescriptive method (Annex G).
A finite element model of a raft, in which you study the load–settlement relationship right up to failure.
Numerical design is also part of the direct method (in the new EC7: design by calculation).
